description: Composite EBSD figure of the 19Al (Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu at.%) alloy, laid out in three rows for the three aging conditions — (a) 525 °C/10 h, (b) 600 °C/3 h, (c) 650 °C/6 h — each row pairing an inverse pole figure (IPF) map, carrying the standard 001/101/111 colour-wheel key, with an adjacent phase map whose legend lists BCC, α-Mn, β-Mn and FCC. Within each row a lower-magnification map (scale bars 500 μm in a, 100 μm in b, 200 μm in c) is followed by a magnified view (10 μm in a2; 5 μm in b2 and c2). In (a) the phase map is dominated by an α matrix (annotated "α") with a thin green β-Mn network along the grain boundaries. In (b1)/(c1) the phase map is almost entirely green β-Mn. The magnified (b2) map is annotated "New FCC phase" with arrows pointing to small violet particles, while the magnified (c2) map shows red particles inside green β-Mn annotated "New BCC phase". Together the panels show the α→β-Mn transformation advancing with aging temperature and the emergence of new BCC and FCC precipitates inside β-Mn.

subfigures.description: Lower-magnification EBSD pair for 525 °C/10 h: an IPF map (500 μm scale bar) with a few large equiaxed grains in many orientations, beside a phase map in which a red matrix carries a thin green β-Mn network along grain boundaries.

Magnified EBSD pair (10 μm scale bar) for 525 °C/10 h: IPF map with coarse pink/cyan/orange orientation domains and a phase map whose continuous red matrix is lettered 'α', with green β-Mn and minor magenta regions.
EBSD pair for 600 °C/3 h (100 μm scale bar): IPF map showing many differently coloured grains beside a phase map that is essentially uniform green (β-Mn).

Magnified EBSD pair for 600 °C/3 h (5 μm scale bar): IPF map with large orange and blue orientation domains, and the matching phase map showing those domains plus green β-Mn and small violet particles labelled 'New FCC phase' by arrows.
EBSD pair for 650 °C/6 h (200 μm scale bar): IPF map of many small grains and a phase map that is uniform green (β-Mn).
Magnified EBSD pair for 650 °C/6 h (5 μm scale bar): uniform red IPF map beside a phase map of green β-Mn containing dispersed fine red particles annotated 'New BCC phase'.

observations.observation: The group is EBSD: each row contains an inverse pole figure map with a 001/101/111 colour-wheel key and an accompanying phase map whose legend box lists the entries BCC, α-Mn, β-Mn and FCC.
Readable scale bars: 500 μm and 10 μm in row a, 100 μm and 5 μm in row b, 200 μm and 5 μm in row c, so each condition is shown once at low and once at high magnification.
The 525 °C/10 h phase map (a) is matrix-dominated with a thin green β-Mn network decorating the grain boundaries, and the magnified map letters the matrix 'α'.
The 600 °C/3 h and 650 °C/6 h phase maps (b1, c1) are essentially uniform green β-Mn, with no visible α grain-boundary network.
Arrows labelled 'New FCC phase' point to small violet/magenta particles in the magnified 600 °C/3 h phase map (b2).
Arrows labelled 'New BCC phase' point to red particles dispersed in the green β-Mn of the magnified 650 °C/6 h phase map (c2).
The caption states the three rows are the 19Al alloy aged at (a) 525 °C for 10 h, (b) 600 °C for 3 h and (c) 650 °C for 6 h.
The caption states that (a1–c1) are the EBSD results of the magnified views of (a2–c2); this ordering is the reverse of the scale bars I can read and is reported here with low confidence.
The citing text states that after aging the 19Al alloy at 525 °C for 10 h only a small amount of β-Mn precipitated (12.1 %).
The citing text states that in the sample aged at 650 °C for 6 h the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn and a great amount of new BCC phase was observed within the β-Mn.
The citing text describes the new precipitates within β-Mn as having BCC (red highlighted) and FCC (pink highlighted) crystalline structures.

The citing text states that the EBSD results (Figs. 4, 5 and 6) reveal the presence of the BCC phase within the β-Mn and that the FCC Cu-rich phase content between β-Mn interfaces decreases with increasing Al content.
The IPF maps show many differently coloured grains without a single dominant colour, i.e. no strong preferred orientation is visually apparent in any of the rows.

measured_quantities: crystal orientation / inverse pole figure colour (001–101–111)
unreadable_items: Legend swatch colours cannot be matched unambiguously to the phase names (BCC / α-Mn / β-Mn / FCC) at the supplied resolution
The caption's subscript ordering '(a1-c1) are the magnified views of (a2-c2)' contradicts the scale bars, which give the larger values to the first panel of each row
Fine phase detail inside the small particles in (b2) and (c2) is below the readable resolution
